items.name: Glass Beach
items.concept: A cool silver shore with ribbons of tiny frosted sea-glass pebbles and an angled coastline.
items.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Project asset: square equipable creature background for the Critters mobile game.
Input image 1 is the current background to redesign and the authoritative ART STYLE reference. Rebuild its scenery and composition substantially as specified; preserve its thick BLACK cartoon outlines, rounded simple forms, broad flat color areas, restrained two-tone cel shading, and friendly hand-drawn game-world style. Outline major foreground and midground shapes boldly in real near-black, about 6–10 px at a 1536 px canvas. Do not drift into painterly realism, soft edge painting, intricate textures, or hairline outlines.
Deliver one clean 1536 x 1536 square opaque background, full bleed. No character, animal, creature, UI, lettering, labels, watermark, border, or built-in character shadow.
GAME COMPOSITION: The game crops away the upper 39% in its wide view, so the scene's identifying shapes must read within y=42–78% of the square, not only in the sky. It may crop the sides on narrow stages too. Reserve the lower central area x=32–68%, y=75–98% as a visually calm continuous flat standing surface, with feet at y=93%. Keep depth/landmark shapes behind that space. The eventual creature is about 20% of image width, so ordinary pebbles, flowers, loose debris, and other small objects must remain genuinely tiny. No giant decorative items. Keep clean separate silhouettes suitable for later light animation.
REDESIGN GLASS BEACH: Replace the tropical golden-sand cove composition with a distinctive open, cool-toned sea-glass shoreline. Silvery mauve-gray sand, gentle dusky aqua sea, and a sweeping curved/diagonal tideline from middle-left into the right midground. Use an open distant horizon and a few low dark slate shelves on one side, rather than enclosing cliffs and large green bushes on both sides.
The defining feature is several graceful ribbons of SMALL rounded frosted sea-glass pebbles washed up along the tideline and side edges: mint, teal, lavender, pale blue and a little amber. Their collective colored bands should be recognizable at thumbnail size. Each actual pebble is only about 8–18 px on a 1536 image, many separated tiny chips grouped into simple color patches, never large jewel boulders or crystals. Leave the central bottom standing patch mostly plain gray sand with very few small chips. A thin scalloped foam curve and a broad band of wet reflective sand should make an asymmetric shoreline shape visible in the bottom 60% of the artwork. Soft cool morning light, not a golden tropical cove. Avoid flashy sparkles, glass monoliths, oversized pebbles, seashells, buildings, and trees. Preserve strong black contours on slate, shore and wave shapes.

A broad flat dark ash-gray rock terrace fills the lower third for the creature.
The ridge profile, a few short hexagonal basalt columns, and two pale curling steam plumes from small side fissures should remain recognizable at y=45–78%. Use charcoal, dusty plum, muted brick-red and sulfur-ochre mineral stains, with only two or three SMALL orange ember cracks at the side edges. The overall image should read as cool ash-colored mountains and geothermal steam, not an orange lake or a vast lava field. A distant smoking volcanic cone is allowed but cannot be the only identifying feature. Keep rock landforms bold and simple, strong thick black outlines, limited flat cel shading. Give the lower central surface ample quiet open room. No lava sea, no eruption wall, no flames across the floor, no giant foreground framing pillars on both sides, no sharp rocks in the creature standing area.

These are SNOW-ENCRUSTED TREES, not literal ghosts; no faces, eyes or humanoids.
Make an asymmetric cluster of three rime sculptures on one shoulder of a broad snow crest, and a smaller more distant cluster opposite, with open powder-blue mist and a receding ridge visible between them. Their sculptural lower halves and full smaller trees should clearly occupy the middle y=45–76% so the feature survives top cropping. A curved snow cornice and simple wind-carved ripple bands create a flowing ridge line across the midground. Keep the bottom central third a broad safe level snowy standing patch, not a cliff edge or hollow. Palette warm ivory-white, icy pale turquoise and muted blue-gray shadows; distinguish it strongly from a conventional blue-violet snowy pine forest. Thick near-black contours on the main white sculptural shapes and snowbanks, simple two-tone shading, minimal texture. No ordinary triangular green Christmas trees, no branch-by-branch detail, no falling snow clutter, no sharp ice-spike field.

Curving bands of taller golden grass lean gently in one breeze direction along the side margins and middle distance, not enclosing the scene. Keep vegetation clusters modest in scale: individual blades and seed heads far smaller than the creature, grass banks as landscape bands. Sunlit, open and welcoming. Create interest through flowing land/grass shapes and the asymmetrical blue stream, not lots of objects. Strong black outlines on readable grass clumps, stream banks and a few tiny field stones; broad flat two-tone shading. No fences, buildings, roads, giant flowers, giant wheat heads, mountainous valley, dense corner bushes, or rocky/tree archway.
